prompts.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. EDIT the supplied concept reference into extremely crisp and SIMPLE LOW-RESOLUTION PIXEL SPRITES. The reference supplies ONLY creature identity, NOT its painted shading. The previous attempt looked like a detailed illustration; correct that decisively. Use coarse 8-bit/16-bit handheld game sprite construction, each whole creature composed on approximately 32 by 32 logical pixels. Enlarge each logical pixel as a uniform large square so square blocks are unmistakable. Hard staircase contours, flat solid-color rectangular clusters, a single dark pixel outline, no smooth curves, NO antialiasing, NO gradients, NO airbrush, NO texture/noise, NO detailed scratches, NO subpixel edge highlights, NO painted metallic shading. Maximum 12 flat colors across the ENTIRE sheet; at most TWO shades per material. Prioritize clean silhouette over detail. FOUR static views of ONE creature arranged in an exact 2 COLUMNS by 2 ROWS square layout. Top left DOWN-facing toward camera, top right LEFT-facing, bottom left RIGHT-facing, bottom right UP-facing away. All viewed from same elevated TOP-DOWN RPG perspective. One sprite per equal square cell with plenty of transparent padding, same scale, identical anatomy and palette. Rear view has NO face on the back. No animation, no duplicate large/small versions, no extra enemies, no text, no labels, no shadows, no ground, no border, no scenery. TRANSPARENT background. Completely redesign the rendering as tiny economical sprite art; do not simply pixel-filter a large painting. Target ONLY the LEFT creature B1 FENDA in the reference. Preserve lean hunching biped, wedge head with one tiny amber vertical slit, two long curved scythe forearms, two short bent digitigrade legs, ash-brown simple armor and muted rust-red joints. Forearm blades form a wide open silhouette. Simplify to roughly five major shell shapes; no metal bands or tiny facets. Both feet and both scythes visible in front view. Adult frightening enemy, never cute.
